# Company 097 — Indirect Tax / Sales-Tax Compliance Autopilot

**Company ID:** `company:future:097`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:097`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-097-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no tax filing, registration, remittance, customer tax change or legal/tax attestation.

## Business identity
Purpose: provide deterministic infrastructure for indirect-tax determination, evidence, reconciliation, registration tracking and filing preparation across jurisdictions while routing ambiguous classifications to qualified review.

Problem: sales tax, VAT, GST and related indirect taxes depend on jurisdiction, nexus/thresholds, product/service classification, customer exemptions, marketplace rules, place-of-supply and rapidly changing rates/rules.

Value: accurate tax determination inputs, explainable jurisdiction/classification evidence, cleaner reconciliation and deadline control without pretending software replaces tax professionals.

## Complete product tree
Nexus/Threshold Monitor; Jurisdiction Registry; Product/Service Taxonomy; Taxability Classification; Rate Engine Adapter; Exemption Certificate Manager; Customer Tax Status; Place-of-Supply Engine; Marketplace-Facilitator Rules; Invoice Tax Calculator; Refund/Credit Adjustment; VAT/GST/Digital-Service Packs; Registration Tracker; Filing Calendar; Return Preparation Workspace; Tax Reconciliation; Audit Evidence; Rule/Rate Change Monitor; Scenario Simulator; API/SDK; White-Label/OEM; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Regional/Industry Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree
Features: seller/entity, jurisdiction, registration/status, threshold period, transaction/customer/product/service, tax category, exemption, place of supply, rate source/version, taxable base, tax amount, marketplace responsibility, invoice/refund refs, filing period, reconciliation, assumption/confidence, evidence and review state.

Customers: ecommerce, SaaS/digital services, marketplaces, multi-state/multi-country businesses, manufacturers/distributors, accounting/tax firms, ERP/billing providers and enterprises.

Verticals: physical goods, digital products, SaaS, services, subscriptions, marketplaces, food/grocery, manufacturing, telecom-like services and cross-border digital services. Each needs separate validated packs.

## Brain capability tree / architecture
Brain may interpret product descriptions, surface candidate classifications and explain ambiguous rules. Tax calculation/enforcement must use validated deterministic rule/rate sources. Brain cannot make unsupported legal nexus determinations or submit filings.

Architecture: jurisdiction/rule registry, entity/registration graph, tax-category ontology, transaction normalization, deterministic calculation adapter, exemption store, threshold/nexus tracker, marketplace responsibility rules, filing-period ledger, reconciliation engine, provenance/evidence and protected filing/remittance gates.

## Agent tree
Jurisdiction Monitor; Nexus/Threshold Agent; Product Classification Agent; Exemption Agent; Marketplace Rule Agent; Tax Calculation QA Agent; Registration Tracker; Filing Prep Agent; Reconciliation Agent; Change Monitor; Audit/Evidence Agent; Tax-Professional Review Router.

## Deterministic services
Jurisdiction/date rules; threshold arithmetic; rate/version lookup; taxable-base calculation; exemption validation; place-of-supply rules; marketplace responsibility; rounding; refund adjustments; filing-period aggregation; reconciliation hashes; deadline scheduler.

## Workflow tree
Ingest entity/registration/product/customer/transaction facts → resolve jurisdiction/place of supply → verify tax category/exemption → apply exact rule/rate version → calculate tax → record evidence → reconcile invoice/payment/refund/marketplace data → monitor thresholds/registration need → prepare return/workpaper → route ambiguity to qualified review → filing/remittance only through separately authorized workflow → preserve receipt/evidence.

## Integrations / API / data
Billing/checkout, ecommerce/marketplaces, ERP/accounting, payments, product catalogs, customer/exemption systems, tax-rate/rule providers, government portals via lawful interfaces, document storage and calendars. Data: entities, registrations, jurisdictions, products/categories, customers/exemptions, transactions, rates/rules, calculations, filings/workpapers and evidence.

## Monetization / distribution
Transactions, jurisdictions, entities, registrations, filings/workpapers, seats, enterprise/private, API/OEM, regional packs and managed preparation support. Distribution through ecommerce/billing/ERP/accounting/tax ecosystems.

## Security/privacy/compliance
Financial/customer data is sensitive. Rule sources/versioning, no fabricated tax certainty, qualified review for ambiguity, auditability, role separation, protected submissions/remittances, jurisdiction-specific privacy/retention and no claim to replace tax professionals.

## Failure / edge cases
Threshold changes, retroactive rules, marketplace facilitator split responsibility, mixed bundles, subscriptions across periods, exemption expiry, customer location ambiguity, tax-inclusive pricing, currency/rounding, refunds after filing, cross-border place-of-supply, digital-service rules, registration pending, tax-engine outage. Unknown classification must remain explicit.

## Scale / overlap
Single-region tax helper → multi-jurisdiction compliance platform → global indirect-tax infrastructure. Overlap #69 usage billing, #85 revenue leakage, #86 payment reconciliation, #99 data contracts. #097 owns tax determination/compliance workflow.

## Classification
**DESIGN NOW:** jurisdiction/region metadata, versioned rule sources, deterministic financial calculations, legal/tax review state, deadlines, protected filing/remittance classes and evidence lineage.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center financial/policy architecture should support jurisdiction-aware rule packs and keep calculated tax, filed tax and paid tax as separate truth states.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** validated tax-rule provider abstraction, jurisdiction/entity registry, product-taxonomy hooks and deadline/reconciliation engine.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** commercial tax packs, government/provider connectors, customer workflow and pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** global rule/rate graph and high-volume multi-region computation.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block
1. Product Tree: nexus/jurisdictions/classification/rates/exemptions/place-of-supply/marketplace/invoice/refund/VAT-GST/registration/calendar/filing/reconcile/audit/API.
2. Feature Tree: entity/jurisdiction/registration/threshold/transaction/customer/product/category/exemption/rate version/tax/marketplace/period/evidence.
3. Customer Tree: ecommerce/SaaS/marketplace/multiregion/manufacturer/accounting/ERP/enterprise.
4. Vertical Tree: goods/digital/SaaS/services/subscriptions/marketplaces/grocery/manufacturing/telecom-like/cross-border.
5. Brain Tree: classification/explanation; tax calculation and filing rules deterministic/qualified-review backed.
6. Agent Tree: jurisdiction/nexus/classification/exemption/marketplace/calculation QA/registration/filing/reconcile/change/evidence/review.
7. Service Tree: rules/threshold/rates/tax base/exemption/place-of-supply/rounding/refunds/aggregation/reconcile/deadlines.
8. Workflow Tree: facts→jurisdiction→classification→calculate→evidence→reconcile→threshold/registration→prepare→review→authorized filing.
9. Integration Tree: billing/ecommerce/ERP/payments/catalog/customers/tax providers/portals/docs/calendar.
10. Data Tree: entities/registrations/jurisdictions/products/customers/transactions/rules/calculations/workpapers/evidence.
11. API Tree: classify/calculate/nexus/status/reconcile/workpapers/evidence.
12. Monetization Tree: transactions/jurisdictions/entities/filings/seats/enterprise/API/packs/managed.
13. Distribution Tree: ecommerce/billing/ERP/accounting/tax/OEM.
14. Automation Tree: determination/reconciliation/deadlines automatic; legal classification ambiguities and submissions/remittance gated.
15. Moat Tree: validated rule packs, classification corpus, jurisdiction graph, reconciliation accuracy.
16. Platform Tree: tax engine→indirect-tax OS→global tax infrastructure.
17. Risk Tree: wrong tax/late filing/legal overclaim/data leak/rule staleness/duplicate remittance.
18. Scale Tree: jurisdiction→multiregion enterprise→global.
19. Spinoff Tree: exemption-certificate/registration intelligence modules; billing/reconciliation remain adjacent.
20. Command Center Dependencies: financial governor, jurisdiction/policy packs, product/catalog metadata, evidence, protected actions, scheduler.
21. Design-Now Requirements: jurisdiction, effective-version and regulated-review metadata reusable across portfolio systems.
22. Build-Now Requirements: financial truth model must distinguish calculated, reported/filed, payable and paid/remitted states.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: commercial tax content/government filing connectors/global rate network.
24. Autonomous Mature State: routine tax determination, threshold monitoring and reconciliation run continuously; qualified humans resolve ambiguous classification and authorize filings/remittances.

## Saturation result
Further branches converge into billing, reconciliation, product classification and regulatory monitoring already represented.

# Company 098 — Data Sovereignty & Workload Routing Platform

**Company ID:** `company:future:098`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:098`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-098-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no customer workload migration, provider activation, region change or production routing.

## Business identity
Purpose: route storage, compute and AI workloads according to jurisdiction, residency, sovereignty, privacy, customer contract, security, latency, cost and provider constraints.

Problem: modern systems spread data through databases, backups, logs, AI inference, embeddings, analytics, agents and support tools; a single provider default can violate customer/region policies or make later sovereignty retrofits extremely expensive.

Value: machine-enforced regional placement, prohibited-region blocking, explainable routing, compliant failover and migration planning without assuming every workload may run everywhere.

## Complete product tree
Data/Workload Classifier; Jurisdiction/Residency Policy Registry; Provider/Region Capability Catalog; Storage Router; Database Router; Backup Router; AI Inference Router; Training/Batch Router; Analytics/ETL Router; Agent/Browser-Worker Router; Search/Embedding/Vector Router; Log/Telemetry Router; Support-Data Router; Regional Failover; Prohibited-Region Gate; Contract/Customer Policy Overlay; Topology Dashboard; Policy Simulator; Migration Planner; Evidence/Audit; API/SDK; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Sovereign-Cloud Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree
Features: workload/data ID, company/customer/tenant, data/sensitivity class, jurisdiction, required/allowed/prohibited regions/providers, contract/policy version, encryption/KMS location, model/provider capability, storage class, latency/cost limits, failover regions, current placement, desired placement, decision reason, evidence and migration state.

Customers: enterprises, SaaS, AI/data platforms, regulated organizations, multinational businesses, government/public-sector systems, cloud/platform providers and MSPs.

Verticals: AI inference, healthcare admin, finance-adjacent, government, HR, consumer privacy, enterprise analytics, support/CRM, software telemetry and global SaaS.

## Brain capability tree / architecture
Brain may interpret contracts/policy text and propose topology/migration plans. Runtime routing must be deterministic from versioned policy and verified provider/region capabilities. Architecture: data/workload registry, jurisdiction/policy ontology, provider-region capability registry, deterministic constraint solver, sensitivity/retention metadata, network/topology model, routing decision ledger, failover policy, migration planner and audit.

## Agent tree
Workload Classifier; Policy Mapping Agent; Provider/Region Analyst; Topology Agent; Routing Planner; Sovereignty QA Agent; Failover Agent; Migration Planner; Cost/Latency Analyst; Incident Agent; Audit/Evidence Agent.

## Deterministic services
Policy precedence; region/provider allow-deny; data-class constraints; capability matching; KMS/encryption constraints; latency/cost ceilings; deterministic route ranking; failover eligibility; placement verification; migration checkpoints; immutable decision evidence.

## Workflow tree
Register workload/data → classify sensitivity/jurisdiction/customer contract → resolve exact policy version → enumerate eligible providers/regions → remove prohibited placements → rank remaining routes under latency/cost/security constraints → route/store/process → verify actual placement → on outage select only policy-compliant failover → reconcile drift → plan protected migration when policy/provider changes.

## Integrations / API / data
Cloud/storage/database providers, AI/model gateways, KMS/vault, data catalogs, ETL/analytics, vector/search systems, logging/observability, browser/agent runtimes and contract/customer policy systems. Data: workload metadata, policy, provider capabilities, placement and decision evidence; customer raw payload need not be centralized.

## Monetization / distribution
Workloads/data stores/regions/providers, routing decisions, seats, enterprise/private, sovereign-cloud packs, API and managed architecture. Distribution via cloud/data/AI/security/compliance ecosystems.

## Security/privacy/compliance
Fail closed when residency is unknown, never treat cost as stronger than legal/security constraint, regional credentials and encryption keys isolated, no silent cross-region failover, immutable evidence and explicit customer-contract precedence. Product supports policy implementation; legal interpretation may need qualified review.

## Failure / edge cases
Provider region outage, service unavailable in required region, policy conflict, customer changes residency requirement, backup replicated globally by default, support vendor accesses data cross-border, model route lacks regional guarantee, DNS/CDN/logging leak, encryption key hosted elsewhere, migration partially completed, data derived into embeddings/cache.

## Scale / overlap
Single workload router → enterprise sovereignty control plane → multi-cloud global workload policy fabric. Overlap #68 model routing, #76 PII classification, #78 retention, #94 lineage. #098 owns jurisdiction-aware placement/routing.

## Classification
**DESIGN NOW:** region/jurisdiction/provider/location metadata, workload/data classification, policy precedence, compliant failover, provider capability registry and placement evidence.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center provider/data/artifact/Brain/Agency contracts must carry region/residency constraints now or later retrofit will be expensive.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** portfolio company deployment/data-store registry must require region/provider policy before public launch.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** commercial multi-cloud routing/migration product.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** global multi-provider topology optimization and sovereign-cloud network.

1. Product Tree: classifier/policy/provider catalog/storage/DB/backup/AI/training/analytics/agents/search/logs/support/failover/gate/topology/simulation/migration/API.
2. Feature Tree: workload/company/customer/data class/jurisdiction/allowed-prohibited/provider/KMS/latency/cost/failover/placement/reason/evidence.
3. Customer Tree: enterprise/SaaS/AI-data/regulated/multinational/government/cloud/MSP.
4. Vertical Tree: AI/health admin/finance/government/HR/consumer privacy/analytics/support/telemetry/global SaaS.
5. Brain Tree: contract/policy interpretation and planning; runtime placement deterministic.
6. Agent Tree: classifier/policy/provider/topology/routing/QA/failover/migration/cost/incident/evidence.
7. Service Tree: precedence/allow-deny/class constraints/capability/KMS/ceilings/ranking/failover/placement/checkpoints/evidence.
8. Workflow Tree: classify→policy→eligible routes→filter→rank→route→verify→compliant failover→reconcile/migrate.
9. Integration Tree: cloud/storage/DB/models/KMS/catalog/ETL/vector/logging/agents/contracts.
10. Data Tree: workloads/policies/provider capabilities/placements/decisions/migrations/evidence.
11. API Tree: classify/evaluate route/place/verify/failover/simulate/migration/evidence.
12. Monetization Tree: workloads/stores/regions/providers/decisions/seats/enterprise/API/managed.
13. Distribution Tree: cloud/data/AI/security/compliance/OEM.
14. Automation Tree: route/verify/failover automatic only within hard regional policy; migrations protected.
15. Moat Tree: provider-region capability graph, policy packs, topology history, compliance evidence.
16. Platform Tree: router→sovereignty control plane→global policy-aware workload fabric.
17. Risk Tree: unlawful placement/silent failover/derived-data leakage/wrong policy/provider misrepresentation.
18. Scale Tree: workload→enterprise→global multi-cloud.
19. Spinoff Tree: AI residency router/backup sovereignty modules; model routing/data lineage remain adjacent.
20. Command Center Dependencies: provider registry, sensitivity/region metadata, deployment factory, resource governor, lineage, policy, audit.
21. Design-Now Requirements: every provider-backed resource and AI/context/artifact operation can declare allowed/prohibited regions/providers.
22. Build-Now Requirements: add residency/region policy fields to Command Center provider, data, artifact, model, worker and deployment contracts before later categories proliferate them.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: commercial customer routing/topology/migration engine.
24. Autonomous Mature State: workloads stay in compliant locations and fail over only to eligible regions; humans handle policy/legal ambiguity and major migrations.

# Company 099 — Machine-Enforced Data Contract Platform

**Company ID:** `company:future:099`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:099`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-099-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no customer runtime enforcement or production schema mutation.

## Business identity
Purpose: define and enforce machine-readable contracts between data producers and consumers covering schema, semantics, quality, freshness, security, privacy, retention, compatibility and ownership.

Problem: schemas alone do not capture what fields mean, how fresh/complete data must be, who owns it, what uses are allowed or how breaking changes affect applications, analytics, models and agents.

Value: explicit producer/consumer expectations, CI/runtime validation, safer evolution, dependency awareness and data quality/policy enforcement before bad contracts become outages or AI errors.

## Complete product tree
Contract Registry; Schema Registry; Semantic/Unit Contract; Freshness/Latency SLA; Completeness/Quality Contract; Ownership/Stewardship; Privacy/Security/Allowed-Use Contract; Retention Contract; Version/Compatibility Engine; Producer SDK; Consumer SDK; CI Contract Tests; Runtime Validation/Quarantine; Drift Monitor; Dependency/Consumer Graph; Change Proposal/Negotiation Workflow; Generated Documentation; Migration Guidance; Incident/Violation Console; API/CLI; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Domain Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree
Features: contract ID/version, producer/consumer, dataset/event/API object, schema/types, required/optional fields, semantic definitions, units, enums, freshness/latency, completeness, quality thresholds, ownership, sensitivity, allowed purposes, retention, SLA, compatibility range, deprecation, violations, evidence and acceptance state.

Customers: data teams, software platforms, analytics/BI, ML/AI teams, event-driven systems, enterprises, data-product providers, marketplaces and internal platform teams.

Verticals: finance data, ecommerce/order events, SaaS telemetry, marketing analytics, logistics, IoT/manufacturing, healthcare administrative data, AI/RAG/model inputs and internal APIs/events.

## Brain capability tree / architecture
Brain may help author semantic definitions, detect contradictory requirements and propose migration plans. Enforcement of schemas, thresholds, allowed uses and compatibility must be deterministic from the exact contract version.

Architecture: contract/ontology registry, version graph, schema validators, semantic/unit definitions, quality/freshness evaluator, policy/sensitivity hooks, dependency graph, CI/runtime gateway, violation ledger, negotiation/change workflow and provenance/evidence.

## Agent tree
Contract Authoring Assistant; Schema Agent; Semantic/Unit Agent; Quality/SLA Agent; Privacy/Policy Agent; Compatibility Agent; Producer QA Agent; Consumer Impact Agent; Change/Migration Planner; Violation/Incident Agent; Documentation Agent.

## Deterministic services
Schema/type validation; enum/required checks; units; freshness clocks; completeness/quality formulas; purpose/retention checks; semver/compatibility; contract lookup/version pinning; violation quarantine; dependency graph; idempotent acceptance and audit.

## Workflow tree
Producer proposes/updates contract → resolve owners/consumers → specify schema/semantics/SLAs/privacy/retention → validate contract consistency → consumers review compatibility → version/accept → CI producer and consumer tests → runtime data/event validated against exact version → violation blocks/quarantines/alerts per policy → change negotiation/migration → deprecate old version with evidence.

## Integrations / API / data

# Company 100 — Legacy Software Modernization Autopilot

**Company ID:** `company:future:100`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:100`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-100-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no customer code transformation, migration, deployment, cutover or production mutation.

## Business identity
Purpose: analyze aging software and automate as much of its safe understanding, documentation, modernization planning, transformation, verification and staged cutover as technology and evidence permit.

Problem: legacy systems hide business rules inside old code, schemas, runtime behavior and undocumented integrations; rewriting without behavioral evidence loses critical functionality while endless patching compounds risk.

Value: evidence-backed system understanding, explicit modernization choices, reusable compatibility tests, incremental transformation and safer cutover/rollback.

## Complete product tree
Repository/System Discovery; Architecture Reconstruction; Dependency Inventory; Runtime/Environment Discovery; Database/Data-Flow Mapping; External Integration Discovery; Code/Call/Control/Data Graph; Business-Rule Extraction; User-Journey Reconstruction; Documentation Generator; Technical-Debt/Risk Assessment; Modernization Strategy Planner; Refactor Assistant; Modularization/Service Extraction; Strangler-Pattern Planner; API Extraction; Containerization; Dependency/Framework Upgrade; Language/Framework Transformation; Frontend Modernization; Database Modernization; Compatibility Adapter Generator; Test/Golden-Master Generator; Migration Script Builder; Behavior Comparison; Performance/Security Comparison; Parallel-Run/Canary Controller; Cutover/Rollback Planner; Continuous Modernization Monitor; API/SDK; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Language/Framework/Industry Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree
Features: system/repo/build/runtime IDs, language/framework/version, dependencies, modules, calls/data flows, schemas, integrations, business rules, user journeys, criticality, risk, test coverage, observed behavior, target architecture, modernization option/rationale, transformation version, compatibility evidence, performance/security baseline, cutover state and rollback point.

Customers: enterprises, governments, software vendors, banks/insurers where appropriate, healthcare administrative systems, manufacturers, logistics firms, universities, utilities, agencies/integrators and organizations with long-lived internal software.

Verticals: mainframe/enterprise apps, old web monoliths, desktop software, internal line-of-business systems, legacy APIs, old database platforms, unsupported language/framework stacks and poorly documented custom systems. Every vertical/language needs bounded capability packs.

## Brain capability tree / architecture
Brain may infer architecture/business-rule hypotheses, generate documentation, propose modernization strategies and create code transformation candidates. It cannot treat inferred behavior as verified truth. Deterministic/static analysis, runtime traces, golden tests, schema/data reconciliation and controlled experiments establish acceptance.

Architecture: repository/artifact ingestion sandbox, multi-language parser adapters, code/call/data graph, runtime trace ingest, dependency/SBOM registry, business-rule evidence model, target-architecture planner, transformation workspace, compatibility layer generator, isolated build/test environments, golden-master/replay harness, migration/reconciliation and protected release/cutover control.

## Agent tree
Discovery Agent; Architecture Analyst; Dependency Agent; Data/Schema Agent; Integration Agent; Business-Rule Analyst; Documentation Agent; Modernization Strategist; Refactor Agent; API/Service Extraction Agent; Database Modernization Agent; Test/Golden-Master Agent; Security Agent; Performance Agent; Migration Agent; Parallel-Run Comparator; Cutover/Rollback Agent; Independent QA Agent.

## Deterministic services
Language parsers; AST/call/data-flow analysis; dependency/SBOM; build reproduction; runtime tracing; schema diff; behavior snapshot/replay; golden test fixtures; deterministic code transforms where safe; compiler/static analysis; compatibility matrix; performance benchmarks; data reconciliation; artifact hashing; canary/rollback state.

## Workflow tree
Authorize discovery → inventory source/build/runtime/data/integrations → reconstruct architecture/behavior with verified-vs-inferred labels → generate docs/risk map → choose modernization strategy → freeze target/spec/version → create isolated transformation increment → build/test/security/performance compare → preserve golden behavior or explicitly approve intentional change → stage parallel/strangler/canary rollout → protected migration/cutover → verify/reconcile → rollback if gates fail → continue incremental modernization with evidence.

## Integrations / API / data
Git/source archives, artifact/package registries, CI/build systems, runtime/APM/observability, databases, queues, file systems, legacy APIs, browsers/desktop automation, cloud/container platforms, issue/document systems and release/deployment tools. Data: source metadata/code refs, graphs, schemas, traces, rules/evidence, modernization plans, transformed artifacts, tests and comparison results. Customer source stays isolated.

## Monetization / distribution
Applications/repos/LOC or complexity bands, analysis/modernization projects, compute/test usage, seats, enterprise/private, language/framework packs, API, managed modernization and outcome/milestone pricing where contractually appropriate. Distribution via enterprise engineering, consultancies/integrators, cloud migration partners and software vendors.

## Security/privacy/compliance
Legacy code often contains secrets, old credentials and regulated data. Sandbox ingestion, secret scanning/redaction, isolated builds, no dependency execution before trust checks, least-privilege runtime probes, protected migrations/deployments, IP/confidentiality controls and complete provenance are mandatory.

## Failure / edge cases
No source code, unbuildable environment, undocumented external system, dynamic/reflection-heavy code, generated code, hardware dependency, unsupported database, proprietary library, hidden batch jobs, manual operator process, race/timing dependency, production-only behavior, incomplete test data, stale docs, intentional bug relied on by users, performance regression, data conversion mismatch.

## Scale / overlap
Assessment tool → modernization factory → continuous legacy transformation platform. Overlap #60 Software Migration Autopilot moves data/config; #100 upgrades/rebuilds software. Also overlaps #42 legacy browser worker, #53 release, #65 QA, #80 dependency risk. #100 owns software-understanding/transformation lifecycle.

## Classification
**DESIGN NOW:** artifact/source provenance, isolated execution environments, code/data/dependency graphs, verified-vs-inferred truth labels, reproducible builds, golden/replay evidence, versioned transformations, migration/cutover/rollback contracts.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center Foundry/Agency/Testing/Deployment/Recovery should be able to coordinate multi-stage modernization without core surgery; reverse-map confirms generic project factories need code-analysis and sandbox capability interfaces, not a legacy-specific implementation now.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** reusable secure code-ingestion sandbox, multi-language analysis plugin interface, transformation/test artifact pipeline and compatibility harness.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** actual modernization product, language/framework packs, customer systems and commercial execution.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** large distributed code-analysis/transformation fleets and ecosystem-specific model/tooling networks.

17. Risk Tree: lost behavior/IP leak/secret exposure/bad transform/data loss/performance/security regression/rollback failure.
18. Scale Tree: one app→enterprise estate→large modernization fleet.
19. Spinoff Tree: architecture reconstruction/golden-master/compatibility adapters can be modules; data migration/browser/release/QA remain adjacent companies.
20. Command Center Dependencies: Foundry, Agency, code/tool sandbox, artifact/provenance, Testing Factory, deployment/recovery, dependency security, resource governor.
